notes:
I couldn't do this research. My one attempt to open the sources failed with a "no more tool calls remaining" error, so I didn't read any pages: not Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit), Precept Austin, Augustine on New Advent, or any of the others.

You asked me to report only what the pages say, give a URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes. Anything I wrote now would come from memory, not the sources, and the URLs wouldn't be checked.

In a new turn, I'd start with these pages (none opened or checked yet):
- **Main verse-by-verse:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-121/, then the Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit Commentary pages for Psalm 121 on biblehub.com, then preceptaustin.org's Psalm 121 page.
- **Baptist:** Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* on Psalm 121, on spurgeon.org or blueletterbible.org.
- **Modern scholarship:** the netbible.org notes on Psalm 121 (for example, on what "the hills" means in v. 1 and the "shade on your right hand" in v. 5).
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** Augustine's *Exposition on the Psalms* on newadvent.org. The Latin Bible numbers this psalm 120, so the page may be listed under that number. Also anything on catholic.com or oca.org.
- **Differences between traditions and popular modern teaching:** targeted searches, for example on whether v. 7 promises freedom from all harm, or preservation of the soul and perseverance.

If any pages don't open or don't cover a verse, I'll leave that point out rather than guess.
